summary: My share of 6 runs went to batch-size / step-count economics. The one big win was run 1: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 at unchanged LRs, 0.997333 -> 0.988763 (commit 816ce84), which all five peers adopted as the base for the rest of the cell. The rest of my family turned out to be closed in every direction: 2**17 is worse (0.996870), and still worse (0.989867) even after a5's window-256 and a1's fast loader removed both the CPU floor and the attention cost, so it is gradient noise and not throughput; a 2**18 -> 2**19 ramp is a wash (0.988930). Two further negatives of mine that saved the group runs: tail weight averaging (EMA/Polyak) is a clear LOSS, +0.0045 measured within a single run (0.988051 averaged vs 0.983536 raw, commit 61f43e3), and MLP expansion 4x -> 3x costs +0.006 (0.988331) even though it does buy 4% more tokens and steps. My best reported number is 0.988051; the same run's raw final weights scored 0.983536, and the cell leader at the time I finished was a4's depth-6/dim-768 at 0.978654. What I would try next: keep pushing a4's width axis (dim 768 -> 896 at depth 6, maybe depth 5/dim 896) and re-test the batch ladder ONCE on the widest shape that still wins -- the 2**18 optimum was measured at 29M matrix params, and it should move up as the matrices get bigger and the step gets slower.
